summary: L-5 cab on Eagle Rock in the Willamette National Forest, built 1933-34 and gone by 1953; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The cab was gone by 1953. No source describes what is at the site today.

events.note: August 8, 1933 Oregon Statesman item says the first little cabin will be built on Eagle Rock; panorama photographs taken October 2, 1933 (Rex's page)
FFLOS and firelookout.com date the L-5 cab to 1934
Gone by 1953; neither source gives an exact removal date

evidence.supports: built by the USFS as an L-5 cab in 1934
evidence.quote: The USFS built this L-5 cab in 1934.

evidence.supports: lookout is in the Willamette National Forest
1933 newspaper item: first little cabin will be built on Eagle Rock
evidence.quote: The first little cabin will be built on Eagle Rock

evidence.supports: item printed in The Oregon Statesman
point is familiar to Breitenbush travelers and plainly seen from the road
evidence.quote: The first little cabin will be built on Eagle Rock which is familiar to all who go to Breitenbush, as the point is to be plainly seen from the road.
October 2, 1933: Panorama photos were taken by Robert Cooper and Reino Sarlin.

evidence.supports: status line only: Rex's page lists the lookout as removed, with no date (absence of remains noted)

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict: the August and October 1933 items on Rex's page vs 1934 on FFLOS and firelookout.com; firelookout.com repeats the FFLOS facts. Coordinates: the FFLOS point (44.77281, -122.0306) and the west_us_lookouts point in the brief (44.7772, -122.0445) are about 1.2 km apart and were not resolved here. No staffing or fire information appears in these sources. Access is unknown; the brief's status and kind stay as recorded.
